text:
Sam R.: Quick flag — customer Vertex Labs paid INV-83421 but the PO on the issued invoice is `VERTEX-EU` instead of `VERTEX-US`. Their AP team is rejecting the invoice for reconciliation. Payment captured 2026-03-15 14:02 UTC via Stripe. Need recommended path (reissue vs credit+rebill) and any tax implications. :thinking_face:

Nora Li: Got it — do we have the gateway txn and whether they consent to rebilling? Also need to confirm whether the customer requires the same invoice number or just a corrected invoice for their records.

Sam R.: Gateway txn: ch_3Lk9X0aB. Customer prefers same invoice number if possible, says their ERPs link off invoice id. They're pushing for a straight reissue rather than a new invoice if it's an option.

Finance Bot: Ledger extract snippet: `INV-83421 | paid | 2026-03-15 | amt: 12,450.00 USD | PO: VERTEX-EU | tax: VAT-exempt`

Maya Chen: Quick note — our usual constraint: once payment is captured, changing invoice metadata (PO number) in-place is only possible if the payment gateway supports editing invoice metadata without triggering accounting adjustments. For Stripe we can update invoice metadata but many customers need the invoice PDF content changed (not just metadata). In that case accounting teams want a credit note + new invoice.

Liam Patel: From finance ops perspective: safest, auditable route is credit note + new invoice (credit+rebill). Steps I recommend: 1) issue a credit note referencing INV-83421; 2) create corrected invoice with PO=VERTEX-US and new invoice id (e.g., INV-83421-R1) that references the credit; 3) attempt to reapply the original payment token to the new invoice if customer authorizes; otherwise record as refund + manual payment. This preserves audit trail and VAT handling.

Maya Chen: If they absolutely require the same invoice number on PDF, we can do a manual override in accounting, but that loses a clean audit trail and might break compliance for some EU customers. Not recommended.

Nora Li: Repro steps for portal bug we saw earlier (mapping wrong company code): 1) create invoice via API with payload `{"customer_id":"cust_993","purchase_order":"VERTEX-US"}`; 2) UI preview shows correct PO; 3) but after saving, webhook handler mutated payload to `VERTEX-EU` when tenant region tag was `eu-west-1`. Suspect a transform in the region mapping lambda.

Nora Li: Quick snippet of the suspicious transform log:
```
INFO 2026-03-15T13:58:04Z transform-lambda - payload.po = VERTEX-US -> mapping.rules.region(eu-west-1) applied -> purchase_order = VERTEX-EU
```

Liam Patel: Thanks — Sam, can you confirm if Vertex gives permission to reapply the captured payment? If yes I can try to re-bill with the existing token and avoid refund. If no, we'll need to refund first then collect payment on the new invoice.

Sam R.: I'll ping the customer right now and ask for authorization to reuse the payment method. Also cc-ing their AP contact for acceptance of INV-83421-R1.

Maya Chen: Dev action: @eng-infra, please check mapping lambda for region->company-code overrides. If that's the bug, we should patch to preserve explicit `purchase_order` from API/UI when present.

Liam Patel: Action items: - I'll prepare the credit note template and draft INV-83421-R1. - If customer approves token reuse, I'll attempt capture and mark ledger accordingly. - If token reuse denied, we'll coordinate refund + manual re-collect.

Sam R.: Customer replied: "We approve rebilling using the same payment method" — asking for ETA.

Liam Patel: I'll start the rebill now. Will post final status here.

Finance Bot: Action recorded: credit_note: CN-83421 created, new_invoice: INV-83421-R1 created (status: pending capture).

Sam R.: Thanks all — will update customer and close once payment captured. :white_check_mark:
